 **PD Mode** — `Unified` serves prefill and decode together. `Prefill` / `Decode` split them into dedicated pools (see [PD disaggregation](#3-4-pd-disaggregation)); `Prefill` ships two strategies, both chunked at 16k. On the 8-GPU platforms (B300 1×8, GB300 2×4), `Default` is TP8 and `Long-Context` is `--pp-size 8 --tp-size 1`. On the 16-GPU platforms (B200 2×8, GB200 4×4), both are `--pp-size 16 --tp-size 1` and differ only in `--mem-fraction-static` (0.85 vs 0.90) — deep PP is the throughput shape there, not just the long-context one (see [Deep PP](#deep-pp-for-prefill)).
 
-**Ascend NPU PD** — both NPU platforms split over the Ascend memory fabric, with `Default` as the only prefill strategy: two symmetric 4-node TP32 pools on the 950PR/DT Series, an asymmetric **2P4D** on the A3 Series (TP16 × PP2 × DP2 prefill, NOSPEC; TP64 × DP4 decode). Pool layouts and the fabric env: [On Ascend NPUs](#npu-pd).
+**Ascend NPU PD** — the A3 Series splits over the Ascend memory fabric, with `Default` as the only prefill strategy: an asymmetric **2P4D** (TP16 × PP2 × DP2 prefill, NOSPEC; TP64 × DP4 decode). Pool layout and the fabric env: [On Ascend NPUs](#npu-pd).

DSPARK proposes 7 draft tokens per step (tune in the Playground) and requires `pp_size == 1` on the shipped recipes, so on B200 it also drops the pipeline and re-lays the same 16 GPUs flat: PP2 × TP8 → TP16, PP2 × DCPEP8 → DCPEP16.
